item.title: Applications of Atomic Catalyst Platforms in Electrochemical Oxygen Evolution
Decoupled Dual‐Stream Seawater Electrolysis Toward Cost‐Effective Green Hydrogen Production
Coupled solar hydrogen production and organic oxidation reactions—Do they add value?
item.description: This commentary discusses the advantages of alternative redox reactions for solar water splitting and explains how these reactions, paired with suitable half-reactions, could add value to photocatalysis and photoelectrochemistry. It also distinguishes these reactions from those involving sacrificial reagents and presents recent findings to highlight directions for future research.

Pt-efficient high-entropy alloy heterojunctions for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis
item.description: We report PtCoFeNiCu-CoFe2O4 heterojunction nanoparticles prepared by carbon-thermal shock. With only 0.74 wt % Pt, the optimized catalyst requires 6.7 mV at 10 mA cm−2 and operates for more than 1,700 h at 500 mA cm−2 in a PEMWE cell. Electrochemical measurements and calculations indicate altered hydrogen adsorption, transport, and desorption. Postmortem analysis reveals partial reconstruction, showing that device durability can persist even when the initial alloy structure evolves.

Chromium-directed surface reconstruction in Hofmann MOFs for efficient oxygen evolution and anion-exchange membrane water electrolysis
item.description: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) often undergo structural reconstruction during oxygen evolution, but controlling this transformation remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate that Cr incorporation into a Hofmann-type MOF regulates local coordination and directs surface-selective reconstruction into active oxyhydroxide species while maintaining framework integrity. This Cr-mediated strategy converts uncontrolled MOF degradation into a controllable activation process, enabling efficient oxygen evolution and high-performance anion-exchange membrane water electrolysis.

item.title: Electronic structure engineering of SrIrO3 via tailorable Turing pattern for efficient acidic OER
item.description: Turing-patterned SrIrO3 stabilizes high-valent Ir for acidic OER. Coupling the self-organized grain-boundary architecture with mechanical strain tunes neighboring Ir interactions and redirects the OER pathway, thereby enabling simultaneously enhanced activity and durability. This work establishes a structurally responsive strategy for oxide electrocatalysis.

item.title: Large-area photoelectrodes and devices for solar hydrogen production
item.description: This review examines the scale-up of photoelectrochemical water splitting from laboratory-scale to large-area photoelectrodes, integrated devices, and outdoor systems. It highlights key challenges arising during scale-up, including nonuniform fabrication, resistive losses, gas crossover and bubble management, and long-term durability. Recent advances in scalable fabrication, reactor and device engineering, and outdoor operation are discussed, together with future priorities for bridging laboratory performance and commercially relevant solar hydrogen production.
